THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.10.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:K CRL.MC NO. 6486 OF 2024  2
Petitioner challenges the FIR in Crime No.748/2024 of Thrissur East Police Station.

According to the de facto complainant, during the period from 28.10.2022 to 31.10.2022, the accused had induced the de facto complainant by promising to obtain purchase orders for medicines from other States and collected an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- towards consultation fee and thereafter failed to procure any order or return the amount and thereby committed the offences under Section 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor, I am of the view that the crime was registered on 29.04.2024 and investigation has not yet completed.
Despite the direction by the Sessions Court to the petitioner to surrender before the Investigating Officer, petitioner has evaded.
The time to surrender was extended by this Court, and still petitioner has not 2024:KER:75334 CRL.MC NO. 6486 OF 2024 surrendered and is evading to appear before the Investigating Officer.

3. Notwithstanding the above, considering the nature of allegations, I am of the view that, it is too premature for this Court to interfere under Section 528 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,
especially since the uncontroverted allegations in the FIR do indicate the commission of offences as alleged.
Hence, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to exercise the inherent powers of this Court to quash the proceedings under 528 of BNSS.
4. While exercising the power under section 528 BNSS (erstwhile section 482 Cr.P.C), it is not proper for this Court to sift or weigh the materials and then come to a conclusion one way or the other.
Reference to the decision in State of Kerala v. O.C. Kuttan (1999 (2) SCC 651) is appropriate in this context.

sentences.text: Similarly, in the decision in State of U.P v. O.P.Sharma (1996 (7) SCC 705) it was observed that High Court should be loath to interfere at the threshold to thwart a prosecution exercising its inherent power and instead must allow the law to take its own course.

2 under section 482 should be exercised sparingly and cautiously and only when the Court is of the 2024:KER:75334 CRL.MC NO. 6486 OF 2024 opinion that there will be a gross miscarriage of justice, should resort be made to such powers.

It is thus trite that the power of quashing criminal proceedings should be exercised with circumspection and that too, in exceptional cases and it is not justified for this Court to embark upon an enquiry as to the reliability, genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR,
final report or even the complaint.

A finding on the veracity of a material relied on by the prosecution in a case where the allegations levelled by the prosecution disclose a cognizable offence is not a consideration for the High Court while exercising its power under S.482 Cr.PC.
This Crl.M.C. is dismissed.
